## Pre-checks

**1. Format.** NMI Articles run ≈ 3,000–5,000 words of main text with ≤ 6–8 display items and a separate
Methods section.

| Item | This manuscript | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Main text (Intro + Results + Discussion) | 7,221 words | **44% over the top of the band** |
| Methods | 3,639 words | separate section, as required |
| Abstract | 200 words | within the 200-word limit, exactly at it |
| Main display items | 6 figures + Table 1 = 7 | within 6–8 |
| Extended Data | 18 tables + 6 figures = **24 items** | **against the portfolio guidance of 10** |
| Supplementary | 3 Notes | fine |
| Reporting Summary | drafted (`docs/REPORTING_SUMMARY.md`) | present |

The Extended Data count is a new finding this round and is the larger of the two format problems: 14 of the
24 items have to move into Supplementary Information before the manuscript can be submitted, and which 14 is
an editorial decision the authors should make deliberately rather than by truncation.

**2. Editorial triage.** *Send out for review.* The central claim — that a cue-conflict shape-bias rate is a
property of a readout rather than of a representation — is a conceptual reframing of a measure the field uses
constantly, and it is now supported in three independent systems (a purpose-built two-stream model, 42 frozen
public networks, and human cortex).

**3. Code availability.** Pass. Repository named with branch and commit, BSD-3-Clause, `requirements.txt`
pinned to versions read from the installed environment, plus `requirements.lock.txt` and
`environment.lock.yml`, an Apptainer definition (`docs/reproducibility/mpk-verify.def`), and a one-command
claim verifier. Checkpoints (≈ 17 GB) are outside the repository with a private referee link offered and a
DOI archive promised at acceptance — acceptable under NMI policy, and the DOI is the outstanding item.

**4. Data availability.** **Partial.** NSD (DUA, registration), the Geirhos cue-conflict stimuli and
trial-level observer responses (CC BY 4.0, both mirrors named), and MiniEcoset are all covered. Three
load-bearing sources are not: **the ILSVRC-2012 validation set**, from which the 10,000-image accuracy gate
subset is drawn for every gated span in Results 2.4 and Extended Data Tables 13–18; **the torchvision
IMAGENET1K_V1/V2 weights** for the 39 ImageNet networks; and **the three Stylized-ImageNet ResNet-50
checkpoints**, on which the paper's new representational claim turns. Carried over unresolved from v5.

**5. DOME / Nature ML checklist.** Audited below; one Partial in D (the availability gap above), no Fails.

**6. Ethics.** No flag. No new human data; two public de-identified releases analysed under their own terms,
with the collecting IRBs named; a sex-and-demographics statement that explains why no disaggregation is
possible rather than ignoring the item; and a constraints-on-generality statement that is specific about the
two convenience samples.

**7. LLM-as-method disclosure.** Methods 4.9 is present, specific and unusually complete: the tool, its role
(coding and drafting assistant, including these referee simulations), the commit-level record, and an explicit
statement that no result, number, figure or statistical decision is produced by it. This is the model other
submissions should follow.

## Consensus Strengths

1. **The central claim is now demonstrated three ways and the readout manipulation is airtight by
   construction.** Nothing is retrained, the network's own head is untouched, w = ½ reproduces the trained
   network exactly, and every gated span is scored on held-out natural images. The affine sweep's obvious
   objection — that the span is a property of the linear head — is answered by a refitted two-layer head that
   preserves 92% of it.
2. **Pre-registration is real and the ledger is complete.** Five plan files, each committed before its
   analysis ran, with outcomes appended and never edited. Across the five, the majority of individual
   predictions failed, and every failure is in the manuscript.
3. **Failures are load-bearing rather than buried.** The diet is less accurate, less robust on four of five
   untrained-on corruptions and a worse predictor of BOLD; the most shape-biased model has the lowest error
   consistency; the cortical prediction fails in all three ImageNet networks; the span model failed four of
   seven predictions. Supplementary Note S1 is an explicit list of claims not made.
4. **The zoo result is properly nulled and properly estimator-checked.** A gain on random 15-dimensional
   subspaces of the same features moves no network's rate by more than 0.076 against labelled spans of
   0.20–0.50, in 42 of 42; and every ranking statistic is now given on both estimators.
5. **Reproducibility surface is above the norm for this literature**: a verifier that re-derives 600+ pinned
   numbers from committed result files, a container definition, three lockfiles, and a single command that
   prints the three recommended shape-bias numbers for any torchvision network.

---

## Consensus Weaknesses

1. **[Format: main text; Extended Data]** 7,221 words against ≈ 3,000–5,000, and 24 Extended Data items
   against the portfolio guidance of 10.
2. **[Results 2.4; ED Table 15; Fig. 6c]** The unit-split cortical index still has no null. In the ImageNet
   networks 0.00–0.02 of units are shape-leaning in absolute terms, so the "shape-leaning half" is the half
   nearest d = 0 and plausibly the less driven one; nothing distinguishes "cortex loads on the texture-leaning
   units" from "cortex loads on the better-driven units". Training set (MiniEcoset v ImageNet) and
   architecture remain confounded across the five networks fitted.
3. **[Abstract; Results 2.4 "What the gain acts on"; ED Table 18]** The new headline — the gain acts on
   texture evidence, and the texture share tracks representational bias more closely than the rate does —
   is not shown to be independent of its own construction, and the abstract compresses two different
   exceptions into one clause.
4. **[Methods 4.2; Results 2.4; ED Table 16]** Three numerical inconsistencies, two of them carried from v5:
   578 v 584 GPU-hours; "every other (VGG-16 past four of the five)"; and a stated span range of 0.20–0.50
   whose lower endpoint is the rounded value of the one network below the 0.20 threshold.
5. **[References]** "Geirhos et al. (2019)" is cited five times and is not in the bibliography.
6. **[Author contributions; CITATION.cff; Data availability]** Placeholder contributions, no funding or
   acknowledgements, placeholder CITATION author, no reserved DOI, and three load-bearing data sources
   unnamed in Data availability.
7. **[Methods 4.8]** A single 1,311-word section carrying five distinct protocols, with `B_S^T y` rendering
   as `B_STy` and "model-vs-human preprocessing" used before it is defined.

## Author Questions (actionable)

1. Is the correlation between the texture share and the probe bias (ρ = −0.81) separable from the shared
   construction of the two quantities? A partial correlation given the two subspaces' variance fractions
   (already stored: 4–15% shape, 20–33% texture) would answer it in an afternoon.
2. Can the unit-split index be calibrated against random or drive-matched halves, so that the surviving
   cortical claim in the two trunks is an index value rather than a sign?
3. Which 14 Extended Data items move to Supplementary Information, and does any main-text claim depend on one
   of them?
4. Should "Geirhos et al. (2019)" be merged into the 2018a entry, or does the Stylized-ImageNet release
   warrant its own reference?
5. Does the forced two-way estimator become the primary estimator for the zoo? Its span ranking is the one the
   evidence decomposition predicts (ρ = 0.95 against 0.59), and the held-out primary estimator's split-to-split
   noise is now measured (ρ = 0.58 between the two spans).

## Code Reproducibility (repo provided; verifier run)

- README adequate: **yes**, with one stale sentence ("in nine frozen networks" against 42 in the manuscript).
- Pinned dependencies: **yes** — `requirements.txt` (versions read from installed metadata, not transcribed),
  `requirements.lock.txt`, `environment.lock.yml`.
- Seeds: **yes**, three per condition, reported per seed and never pooled with subjects.
- Example data / runnable check without a download: **yes** — `verify_new_claims.py` re-derives the pinned
  numbers from committed result files with no dataset and no GPU.
- License + DOI: **BSD-3-Clause present; DOI reserved only at acceptance.**
- Container: **yes**, `docs/reproducibility/mpk-verify.def`.
- Estimated time to reproduce a headline number from the artefacts: **< 1 day** for anything the verifier
  covers; the encoding fits and the 42-network zoo need the private archive.

**Try-to-run note.** A fresh verifier run under the repository's own job script (`slurm/verify_claims.sh`,
job 26510851) was killed at the script's one-hour wall limit after passing 600+ checks; the previous run of
the same script took 35 minutes. Neither figure measures the analysis. `verify_new_claims.check_two_by_two`
imports `shape_bias`, a twenty-line pure-numpy scoring function whose module chain (`cue_conflict` ->
`dkl_frontend` -> `helpers`) imports `torch` at module level, and the interpreter the script pinned sat on a
Lustre scratch filesystem that the group's own job arrays had saturated: a bare interpreter took 37 s to
start there, and `import torch` had not completed after 23 minutes. With the identical environment rebuilt
from the repository's own `requirements.lock.txt` on a filesystem that was not under load, the suite runs
**637 checks in 1 min 35 s with no failures** (job 26511423, 1.5 GB peak RSS), which is what a referee should
expect. The job script now pins that interpreter and requests 4 GB and 20 minutes. The module-level `torch`
imports in `src/` are left in place: they cost nothing once the filesystem is fast, but they would penalise
anyone re-using those modules for CPU-only scoring, and that is worth a line in the repository README.

## Comments to Authors (Nature-style, no recommendation here)

### Summary of key messages

You argue that the cue-conflict shape-bias rate — a number the field reads as a property of a representation
— is a property of a readout over components. You demonstrate it three ways. In a purpose-built two-stream
network whose luminance and chromatic streams end training on opposite sides of the shape–texture boundary,
a single mixing weight over frozen features moves the rate from 0.40 to 0.90, and a refitted nonlinear head
preserves 92% of that span. In 42 frozen public networks with no stream split, one gain on each network's own
shape-predictive subspace moves the rate by 0.20–0.50 while top-1 stays within five points, re-ordering a
quarter of all network pairs, and a random-subspace null moves it by at most 0.076. And in human cortex,
fitted to eight NSD subjects, it is the texture-biased stream whose unique variance carries every extrastriate
region, while behaviour reading out from both is shape-biased — with the mixing weight cortex prefers (0.33)
and the one human choices prefer (0.67) on opposite sides of the trained value.

Around that you show three quantities the field bundles with shape bias coming apart from it — robustness,
trial-by-trial agreement with observers, and representational dimensionality — and you add, post hoc, a
mechanism: the gain moves an ImageNet network toward shape mainly by removing texture evidence rather than by
adding shape evidence, the exception being a network whose bias really is representational.

What the manuscript does not claim is as clear as what it does. The cortical generalisation to ImageNet
networks fails and is reported as a failure; the span model failed four of its seven predictions; the
Stylized-ImageNet "moves least" reading has been withdrawn from the abstract on the strength of your own
estimator comparison. Supplementary Note S1 lists nine claims you decline to make.

### Major comments

**1. The unit-split cortical index needs a null (Results 2.4; Fig. 6c; Extended Data Table 15).** The index
`(U_S − U_T)/(U_S + U_T)` is computed on a median split of units by shape-minus-texture η². In the ImageNet
networks 0.00–0.02 of units are shape-leaning in absolute terms and in your trunks 0.05–0.17, so the
"shape-leaning half" is not a set of shape-selective units; it is the half nearest d = 0. A half of
weakly-differentiated units is plausibly also a less-driven half, and a less-driven band loses a variance
partition. Nothing in the manuscript separates "extrastriate cortex loads on the texture-leaning units" from
"extrastriate cortex loads on the better-driven units". Two controls would settle it: the same index under
random halves of the units, and under halves matched on total η² (or on mean response variance across the NSD
stimuli). Both reuse the stored fits. Relatedly, the five networks fitted confound training set with
architecture — the V1-relative contrast holds in your two MiniEcoset trunks and fails in all three ImageNet
networks — and an ImageNet ResNet-18 or ResNet-34 under the unit rule would separate the two factors with the
architecture held fixed. Neither control is needed for the behavioural claim, which is what makes the paper
relevant to this journal; both are needed before a reader can weigh the cortical one.

**2. The new evidence-decomposition result should be stated more carefully (Abstract; Results 2.4 "What the
gain acts on"; Extended Data Table 18).** Two separate points.

*(a) Independence.* You report that the texture share tracks the probe's representational bias at
ρ = −0.81 [−0.91, −0.62] where the trained rate tracks it at +0.59, with a bootstrap difference in |ρ| of
0.22 [0.04, 0.44], and you read this as the texture share being the better readout-side index of a
representational bias. But the texture share and the probe bias are two functions of the same object: the
1,200-image penultimate feature matrix and the separability of shape and texture labels within it. The texture
share is the head's evidence through `B_T` relative to `B_S`, where `B_S` and `B_T` are the shape and texture
LDA subspaces of those features; the probe bias is how well a linear classifier reads shape against texture
from the same features. A network whose features carry little texture-discriminant structure will have both a
small texture term and a small (less negative) probe bias more or less by construction. The bootstrap over
networks does not address this, because it resamples networks rather than breaking the shared construction.
What would: a partial correlation of the texture share with the probe bias given the two subspaces' variance
fractions (you already store 4–15% shape and 20–33% texture), or a short derivation showing the two are not
monotone functions of a common quantity. As it stands, the claim that the texture share is the *better*
index rests on a difference whose lower bound is 0.04 over a fixed zoo of 38 networks for which you elsewhere
and rightly decline to report p-values.

*(b) The abstract's "except" clause.* "…it acts mostly on texture evidence, except in a Stylized-ImageNet
network whose bias is representational" attributes the exception to the Stylized-ImageNet network. But the
sentence's subject is the 38 ImageNet networks, and the exception among those is ViT-B/32 at a texture share
of 45%; the Stylized-ImageNet network is not one of the 38. Two different facts — one exception inside the
set, one network outside it — are compressed into one clause, and the compression makes the sentence read as
though the Stylized-ImageNet network were the only departure from a clean rule. Split them.

**3. Length and Extended Data count (throughout).** The main text is 7,221 words against a band of roughly
3,000–5,000, and there are 24 Extended Data items (18 tables, 6 figures) against the portfolio guidance of 10
(confirm the current figure against NMI's guide to authors; the Nature portfolio has long set it at 10).
Both are format constraints, not preferences. The length is concentrated in Results 2.4, which at 2,352 words is a
third of the main text and now carries six analyses — the two-stream readout sweep, the cortex-optimal weight,
the six-network subspace test, the 42-network zoo, the evidence decomposition and the unit-rule cortex result; at least two of those are Extended Data
narratives that a reader reaches through a single main-text sentence. On the Extended Data side at least 14 items have to move, so a
shortlist of the clearest candidates — Tables 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 17 and 18 and Figures 2–4, each supporting a
qualification rather than a main-text claim — is not by itself enough; four more must follow it.

**4. Three numerical inconsistencies, two of them raised before.**
*(a)* Methods 4.2 states that the 21 training runs took "578 GPU-hours in total (19.5–51.4 h each, from the
runs' own timing logs)" and, two sentences later, that the scheduler allocated "584 GPU-hours to the 21
training runs". Both may be right — allocated against measured — but the manuscript does not say so, and the
reader is left with two totals for one quantity.
*(b)* Results 2.4 and the Fig. 6b caption both state that "within the gate each network can be moved past the
trained rate of every other (VGG-16 past four of the five)". The parenthesis contradicts the claim. Write
"every network can be moved past at least four of the other five, and five of the six past all five".
*(c)* Extended Data Table 16 gives the gated span as "0.20–0.50 (median 0.30), ≥ 0.20 in 97%". The minimum is
EfficientNet-V2-S at 0.198, so the range's lower endpoint is the rounded value of the single network that
misses the threshold. Give the range to three decimals, or state the exception explicitly.

**5. An unresolved reference (Results 2.4 ×2; Methods 4.8; Extended Data Table 16; Extended Data Fig. 6).**
"Geirhos et al. (2019)" is cited five times, for the three Stylized-ImageNet ResNet-50 checkpoints, and has no
entry in the reference list. The same work appears there as "Geirhos et al. (2018a)" (ICLR 2019), whose
disambiguating letter has no companion "2018b". Since the Stylized-ImageNet networks carry your new
representational claim, this is the one citation a reader will chase.

**6. Statements (Author contributions; CITATION.cff; Data availability).** Author contributions is a bracketed
placeholder; there is no funding or acknowledgements section; `CITATION.cff` carries a placeholder author and
no DOI. Data availability should also name the ILSVRC-2012 validation set and its terms of access (the
10,000-image gate subset is a committed file list, which is the right thing to say), the torchvision
IMAGENET1K_V1/V2 weights, and the three Stylized-ImageNet checkpoints of the Geirhos release.

### Minor comments

- **m1.** Methods 4.8 uses "model-vs-human preprocessing" before defining it; the Resize/CenterCrop
  specification appears later in the same paragraph. Define at first use or drop the phrase.
- **m2.** `B_S^T y`, `B_T^T y` and `B_R^T y` render in the PDF as `B_STy`, `B_TTy` and `B_RTy`. Set the
  transpose as a superscript.
- **m3.** Methods 4.8 is a single 1,311-word block carrying five protocols (subspace rule, unit rule, gate and
  estimators, refit, cortex) plus the evidence decomposition. Sub-head it.
- **m4.** Fig. 4a annotates "0.51 spanned by re-weighting alone" while the text and abstract give 0.40 to 0.90,
  a span of 0.50. Both are defensible (median per-seed span against the seed-mean curve) but the figure and
  the text should say which is which.
- **m5.** Results 2.4: "the two streams alone bracket the integrated readout (0.903 and 0.400 around 0.655)"
  follows a sentence using final-checkpoint values (0.878 / 0.418 / 0.675). Name the checkpoint policy in that
  sentence.
- **m6.** The abstract's "re-ordering a quarter of all pairs" is 27% on the held-out primary estimator and 21%
  on the forced one. Say which.
- **m7.** Extended Data Table 18's caption runs to roughly 700 words and reproduces the whole S-1…S-7 ledger.
  The ledger belongs in the plan file; the caption should say what the table shows.
- **m8.** `slurm/verify_claims.sh` requests one hour. A fresh run of it today was killed at the wall after
  passing 600+ checks (a previous run of the same script took 35 minutes). Raise the limit so a referee
  following the repository does not meet a timeout.
- **m9.** The README says "in nine frozen networks with no stream split at all"; the manuscript tests 42.
- **m10.** Supplementary Note S1's third bullet gives the pre-declared dorsal−ventral interaction as "+0.0245
  on the diet model and +0.0122 (p = .195) without the low-pass front end" — a p-value on the second value and
  none on the first. Give both or neither.

### Notes by criterion

**Technical soundness.** Strong. The readout manipulation is exact rather than approximate: w = ½ reproduces
the trained network bit-for-bit, features do not depend on w, and the gain is an identity on the logits. The
obvious confound — that a refitted head could undo the manipulation — is tested and the span survives. The
encoding analysis replaces a correlational instrument that a general factor had defeated with a variance
partition that is identifiable (canonical correlations from ≈ 0 to 0.93) and whose recovery simulation returns
the true ordering exactly. Degenerate control arms are declared degenerate and excluded from claims rather
than quietly reported.

**Support for conclusions.** Strong for the behavioural and readout claims, which are what the title asserts;
qualified for the cortical one, which the manuscript itself now scopes to the two trunks and the unit rule.
The one place where support has not caught up with the claim is the post hoc evidence decomposition, whose
central correlation is not shown to be independent of its own construction (Major 2a).

**Significance and originality.** The reframing is real and portable. Prior work established that a
representation can hold more shape than behaviour reveals, that the measured rate depends on test design, and
that prompts steer it in VLMs; what is new here is holding the representation exactly fixed and moving the
rate by the readout alone, across 42 public networks, with a null. The three-number reporting standard in the
Discussion, with a one-command implementation, is the part most likely to be adopted.

**Methodology and statistics.** Exemplary in its conservatism: two statistics required to agree before a claim
is made, exact tests at their resolution floor, an enumerable permutation null where one exists,
pre-registered equivalence bounds for the null results, and an explicit, reasoned refusal to claim
multiple-comparison correction rather than a token Bonferroni. Seeds and subjects are never pooled.

**Reproducibility.** Above the norm. A verifier that re-derives 600+ numbers from committed files, three
lockfiles, a container definition, and Methods sections that name the producing module for every reported
number. What is missing is archival: a DOI, a real author list in the citation file, and three data sources in
the availability statement.

**Clarity and presentation.** The weakest axis, and the one the format constraints act on. Beyond length, the
density is uneven: Results 2.4 asks the reader to hold the two-stream sweep, the cortex-optimal weight, two
generality rules, a 42-network zoo and an evidence decomposition simultaneously, and Methods 4.8 answers with
one unbroken block.

**Responsible AI.** Handled well and without boilerplate. Compute and energy are derived from the scheduler's
own accounting with the estimate declared an upper bound and its exclusions named; the LLM-assistance
statement is specific about role, record and responsibility; the constraints-on-generality statement is
concrete about who the two samples are. The gap is administrative, not substantive.

## Confidential Comments to the Editor

**Triage.** Send out. This was never a triage case and is less of one now.

**Significance.** Yes, and I would expect citations within a year — not primarily for the two-stream model,
which is an existence proof, but for the readout-span construction and the three-number reporting standard.
Any group that reports a cue-conflict shape bias can run the authors' one command on their own network, and
the demonstration that a quarter of the field's ranking reverses under an accuracy-neutral readout change is
the kind of result that changes what people report.

**Recommendation.** Minor revision by all three referees; 8.91 on the simulation rubric, inside the Accept
band by score, with no referee at Accept. My reason for not going to Accept is not the science. Between v5 and
this version the authors closed every substantive item raised last round — they rescoped the abstract, fixed
four stale replication statements and a two-seed table cell, added the random-direction null and the
forced-estimator ranking, and withdrew a claim from their own abstract after their own analysis undermined it.
What remains blocking is a manuscript 44% over length with 24 Extended Data items against the portfolio guidance of 10, a
bracketed Author contributions section, a reference cited five times and absent from the bibliography, and two
arithmetic inconsistencies I flagged last round that are still there. None of that requires an experiment.

**What I would ask for at resubmission.** The format cut and the Extended Data triage; the statements and the
DOI; the citation and the three numerical inconsistencies; and the abstract's "except" clause split. I would
mark two things as desirable but not blocking: a calibration of the unit-split index against random and
drive-matched halves, and a partial correlation testing whether the texture-share result survives its own
construction. The first is the last open referee objection on record; the second is an afternoon's work on
stored quantities and would firm up a claim the authors have now placed in their abstract.

**Estimated revision time.** 1–2 months, and realistically two to three weeks if the optional analyses are
declined — almost all of the remaining work is text.

**Suggested additional experiments, with cost/benefit.** (i) Unit-split index under random and drive-matched
halves: reuses the stored NSD fits, two to three days of CPU, and converts the surviving cortical claim from a
sign into a calibrated one. (ii) ImageNet ResNet-18/34 under the unit rule: same pipeline, breaks the
training-set/architecture confound, and is the cleanest way to say whether the V1-relative contrast belongs to
MiniEcoset or to the trunks. (iii) Partial correlation for the texture share: no compute. I would not ask for
anything else; the paper's evidence base is already unusually complete for this literature.

**Reviewer expertise and conflicts.** Simulated panel: ML methodology, visual neuroscience / cue-conflict
behaviour, responsible AI. No conflicts.

## Reflection log

Three refinement rounds were run per persona. R1 initially scored Evidence 3 on the grounds that the
texture-share claim has no null; it was raised to 4 on the reflection that the concern is a missing *analysis*
of quantities already stored, not a missing *experiment*, and that every pre-registered claim in the ledger
does carry its control — the rubric's incompatibility rule is aimed at absent controls, not at absent partial
correlations. R2 initially raised Evidence to 4 in recognition of the random-direction null, then lowered it
back to 3 on the reflection that the null tests the *span*, not the *cortical index*, and its v5 objection was
specifically about the index. R3 considered lowering Recommendation to 3 over the placeholder statements and
did not, because none of them is a scientific defect. No Recommendation moved by ≥ 2 between rounds. As at v4
and v5, the weighted score sits inside the Accept band while the panel is unanimous at Minor revision; the
gap is now entirely format and administration. Word counts are from the compiled source with the v4 counter
(headings, Table 1 and blank lines excluded), recomputed at `9dd1adc`.
